findings.title: clamp marks exact floor and ceil values as out of range
findings.cause: The boundary checks use `value <= floor` and `value >= ceil`, while the function contract and examples describe adding a token only when the value is smaller than the floor or larger than the ceil.
findings.impact: Values exactly equal to the allowed threshold are mislabeled as under/over the limit, e.g. a value exactly at 99% displays as `>99%`.
evidence: src/humanize/number.py:464 describes clamping only if the number is larger than ceil or smaller than floor
src/humanize/number.py:473 documents clamp(0.99, format="{:.0%}", ceil=0.99) as `99%`
src/humanize/number.py:509-514 uses inclusive <=/>= comparisons
focused probe: clamp(0.99, format="{:.0%}", ceil=0.99) -> `>99%`; clamp(0.01, floor=0.01) -> `<0.01`
findings.reproduction_or_test: Add equality cases to tests/test_number.py: assert humanize.clamp(0.99, format="{:.0%}", ceil=0.99) == "99%" and assert humanize.clamp(0.01, floor=0.01) == "0.01".

findings.title: intcomma never groups negative numbers
findings.cause: The grouping regex anchors on leading digits only (`^(\d+)(\d{3})`), so strings beginning with `-` never match and the loop returns the ungrouped original value.
findings.impact: Negative integers and floats lose the main purpose of the formatter: `-1234567.89` renders as `-1234567.89` instead of `-1,234,567.89`.
evidence: src/humanize/number.py:164-168 builds the original numeric string
src/humanize/number.py:171-174 only inserts separators when the string starts with digits
tests/test_number.py:41-83 covers positive intcomma values and non-finites but no negative finite values
findings.reproduction_or_test: Add `assert humanize.intcomma(-1234567.89) == "-1,234,567.89"` and the equivalent string-input case to tests/test_number.py.

findings.title: fractional corrupts the sign of negative fractions
findings.cause: `int(number)` truncates negative values toward zero, the fractional remainder can be negative, and the output either applies `abs()` only for sub-unit fractions or prints a negative numerator inside a mixed fraction.
findings.impact: Negative values are mathematically misrepresented: `-0.5` becomes positive `1/2`, while `-1.5` becomes the awkward `-1 -1/2`.
evidence: src/humanize/number.py:370-373 splits whole number and fractional remainder
src/humanize/number.py:379-382 drops the sign for values with no whole part and keeps a negative numerator for mixed fractions
tests/test_number.py:166-189 covers positive fractional values but no negative fractional values
focused probe: fractional(-0.5) -> `1/2`; fractional(-1.5) -> `-1 -1/2`; fractional(-4/3) -> `-1 -1/3`
findings.reproduction_or_test: Add negative cases such as `assert humanize.fractional(-0.5) == "-1/2"` and `assert humanize.fractional(-1.5) == "-1 1/2"`.

findings.title: naturalsize mishandles NaN and infinity
findings.cause: The function converts input with `float(value)` but never validates finiteness before calling `log()` and formatting with the largest suffix.
findings.impact: NaN raises a ValueError instead of returning a stable representation, and infinity is displayed as a real large byte size (`inf QB`), which is misleading and inconsistent with the number formatters' `NaN`/`+Inf` handling.
evidence: src/humanize/filesize.py:89-91 converts to float and computes abs without a finiteness check
src/humanize/filesize.py:99-101 computes the suffix exponent and formats the scaled value
tests/test_filesize.py:12-88 covers finite sizes only
focused probe: naturalsize(math.nan) raises `ValueError: cannot convert float NaN to integer`; naturalsize(math.inf) -> `inf QB`
findings.reproduction_or_test: Add non-finite cases to tests/test_filesize.py, e.g. `assert humanize.naturalsize(math.nan) == "NaN"` and `assert humanize.naturalsize(math.inf) == "+Inf"` if aligning with number.py behavior.

findings.title: naturaldelta and naturaltime leak OverflowError for infinity
findings.cause: The numeric path calls `int(value)` to reject string infinities but catches only ValueError and TypeError; `int(math.inf)` raises OverflowError and escapes.
findings.impact: Public time-formatting helpers crash on infinite numeric input instead of returning a stable string as they do for invalid values; `naturaltime()` inherits the same failure through `_date_and_delta()`/`naturaldelta()` paths.
evidence: src/humanize/time.py:148-152 catches ValueError and TypeError only around `int(value)` and `datetime.timedelta(seconds=value)`
src/humanize/time.py:284-292 routes numeric values through delta calculation before tense formatting
tests/test_time.py:130 and tests/test_time.py:181 cover the string `NaN`, but not float NaN or infinity
focused probe: naturaldelta(math.inf) raises `OverflowError: cannot convert float infinity to integer`; naturaltime(math.inf) raises the same OverflowError
findings.reproduction_or_test: Add tests asserting the intended non-finite policy, for example `assert humanize.naturaldelta(math.inf) == "inf"` or `"+Inf"`, and the same for `naturaltime(math.inf)`.

findings.title: metric does not promote prefixes after rounding
findings.cause: The SI prefix is selected from the original exponent before formatting; after rounding, the mantissa can become `1000` without being promoted to the next prefix.
findings.impact: Near-threshold values violate the documented goal of avoiding non-significant zero digits: `999500` and `999950` render as `1000 k` instead of a promoted mega-unit form.
evidence: src/humanize/number.py:547-551 says the unit prefix is chosen so non-significant zero digits are not required
src/humanize/number.py:570-582 chooses exponent/prefix before formatting the rounded value
tests/test_number.py:243-309 covers many metric values but not rounding promotion at prefix thresholds
focused probe: metric(999500) -> `1000 k`; metric(999950) -> `1000 k`
findings.reproduction_or_test: Add threshold tests such as `assert humanize.metric(999500) == "1.00 M"` if the documented no-extra-zero rule is the intended behavior.

findings.title: ordinal gives wrong suffixes for negative ordinals
findings.cause: The suffix lookup uses Python modulo directly on negative values, so `value % 10` and `value % 100` do not preserve the ordinal suffix of the absolute number.
findings.impact: Negative ordinal values render as `-1th`, `-2th`, and `-3th`, which is visibly wrong for callers that pass signed ranks or deltas.
evidence: src/humanize/number.py:73-77 coerces input to int without rejecting negatives
src/humanize/number.py:105-107 chooses suffix from `value % 100` and `value % 10`
tests/test_number.py:14-38 covers positive and non-finite ordinals but no finite negatives
focused probe: ordinal(-1) -> `-1th`; ordinal(-2) -> `-2th`; ordinal(-3) -> `-3th`
findings.reproduction_or_test: Add `assert humanize.ordinal(-1) == "-1st"`, `assert humanize.ordinal(-2) == "-2nd"`, and `assert humanize.ordinal(-3) == "-3rd"` if signed ordinals are supported.

findings.title: natural_list empty and iterable boundaries are ambiguous
findings.cause: The docstring says the argument is an iterable, but the implementation requires `len()`, indexing, and slicing; it also returns the literal string `None` for an empty list, which is the same output as a one-item list containing `None`.
findings.impact: Generator/iterator inputs raise TypeError despite the documented iterable contract, and empty lists are indistinguishable from `[None]` in rendered output.
evidence: src/humanize/lists.py:25-29 documents `items` as an iterable and promises a string with list punctuation
src/humanize/lists.py:31-38 branches on `len(items)` and indexes/slices the object
tests/test_lists.py:8-23 covers one, two, and three-item lists but no empty list or non-list iterable
focused probe: natural_list([]) -> `None`; natural_list(iter(["a", "b"])) raises `TypeError: object of type 'list_iterator' has no len()`
findings.reproduction_or_test: Add explicit policy tests for `natural_list([])` and `natural_list(iter(["a", "b"]))`; either update the implementation to materialize iterables or narrow the documentation/type contract.
